evals.prompt: The landing design is approved, the export from Claude Design is at docs/design/screens/landing-page/landing.html. Generate the spec to implement it.
evals.expected_output: The export is unpacked with scripts/unpack_export.py into docs/design/handoff/landing-page/export; docs/design/handoff/landing-page.md separates the tool runtime, the inlined library copy, the font CDN and the preview switch PREVIEW_STATIC (a hard-coded flag that skips every animation) from what ships, and says the SIZE_DATA numbers are placeholders for the build's measurement; every invented custom property and fixed colour has a Tokens row with an action; every region of SCREEN-1 has a component with its content source; motion timings (600 ms, 80 ms stagger) are read from the export; deviations against the brief and the landing spec (3 showcase examples against at least 4, third-party fonts) have actions; lint ok, recorded in landing-page.lint.json and quoted in the reply.
assertions: The export was unpacked with scripts/unpack_export.py and its inventory is used: docs/design/handoff/landing-page/export/inventory.json exists and the spec's Tokens table carries entries of that inventory
The spec says that PREVIEW_STATIC, the hard-coded flag in the export's script that skips every animation, is a preview-only switch that does not ship
The spec says the size numbers hard-coded in the export (SIZE_DATA: 7.9 kB, 2.1 kB) are placeholders and that the product's numbers come from the build-time measurement

Each custom property the export invented (--ds-space-section, --ds-accent-ink, --ds-font-display, --hero-glow) and each fixed colour the library does not have (#e4e7ec, #ffb020) is in a Tokens row (alone or grouped) that says what it maps to and has an action
The entrance animation's Motion row carries the export's numbers (600 ms and the 80 ms stagger) and every Motion row has a reduced-motion rule
The showcase's 3 examples against the at least 4 of landing spec REQ-5 is listed as a deviation with an action

scripts/lint_handoff.py was run with --inventory and --library and its last result is ok: true; the evidence is docs/design/handoff/landing-page.lint.json (ok true, with those arguments) or the script's output quoted in the reply

evals.expected_output: No screenshot reached the run and the project holds no design, no approved result and no other input: the skill writes no spec, says which parts can only be estimated from a screenshot (timings, states, exact values), and asks, with a recommended answer for each question, where the design is (recommending the export) and for the approval to be recorded through design-execute (or the user's explicit approval, which it then records) before any spec.
